authored_by: the C# port, by hand, against the published Rules Reference
notes: Core Set card abilities as data -- docs/card-dsl.md. All 209 Core Set faces have been read; an empty abilities array means the face has no executable text. Later products remain only in datasets/cards and have no executable row. Printed text is quoted from datasets/cards/cards.json, which is extracted rather than authored. The latest Rules Reference decides every behaviour here; where a card's printed words do not settle a case, the note on that card says so and says what was chosen instead.

cards.name: Spider-Man
cards.note: Spider-Sense -- Interrupt: When the villain initiates an attack against you, draw 1 card. 'You' is the attacked player and not the attacked character: rr:attack-enemy-activation.1.4. Printed on the hero face only, which is why the alter-ego face 01001b is a separate card id and carries its own.

cards.name: Peter Parker
cards.note: Scientist -- Resource: Generate a [mental] resource. (Limit once per round.) The sixth generator in the recorded prompt, and the reason that prompt lists six for five payable cards: rr:resource-ability.1 makes one triggerable 'anytime the player who controls the ability is generating resources to pay a cost', so it sits beside the cards in hand rather than in a window. rr:limit counts the use per instance of the ability, which is per card in play -- two Peter Parkers at one table would have one use each.

cards.name: Black Cat
cards.note: Forced Response: After you play Black Cat, discard the top 2 cards of your deck. Add each card with a printed mental resource discarded this way to your hand. The remembered set belongs to this one resolution; rr:printed requires the resource printed on the card, not a modifier.

cards.name: Backflip
cards.note: Interrupt (defense): When you would take any amount of damage from an attack, prevent all of that damage. The attack-damage step carries rr:damage.step.1's imminent-damage condition, and the one-use replacement is consumed by that damage only.

cards.name: Enhanced Spider-Sense
cards.note: Hero Interrupt: When a treachery card is revealed from the encounter deck, cancel its When Revealed effects. rr:cancel.4 leaves the treachery revealed and discarded; only its When Revealed effects are skipped.

cards.name: Swinging Web Kick
cards.note: Hero Action (attack): Deal 8 damage to an enemy. Triggering the Action plays this event under rr:player-turn.5.d, paying its printed cost and discarding it after the chosen enemy is damaged.

cards.name: Spider-Tracer
cards.note: Attach to a minion. Forced Interrupt: When attached minion is defeated, remove 3 threat from a scheme. The chosen scheme is resolved after the defeat interrupt and may be either the main scheme or a side scheme.

cards.name: Web-Shooter
cards.note: Uses (3 web counters). Hero Resource: Exhaust Web-Shooter and remove 1 web counter from it to generate a wild resource. rr:uses-x-type discards the card when its last all-purpose counter is removed.

cards.name: Webbed Up
cards.note: Hero form only. Attach to an enemy. Max 1 per enemy. Forced Interrupt: When attached enemy would attack, discard Webbed Up instead. Then, stun that enemy. The WhenAttackInitiated interrupt precedes attack application, so the newly stunned actor's attack is cancelled by rr:stun.

cards.name: Captain Marvel
cards.note: Rechannel -- Action: spend an energy resource and heal 1 damage from Captain Marvel, then draw 1 card. rr:initiating-abilities.step.5 pays both the resource and healing cost before the draw; rr:limit counts this use once per round.

cards.name: Cosmic Flight
cards.note: Captain Marvel gains the AERIAL trait while this upgrade is in play. Its Hero Interrupt discards Cosmic Flight to prevent 3 of the imminent damage; rr:damage.step.1 opens the interrupt before damage is applied, and rr:prevent reduces rather than cancels an amount larger than 3.

cards.name: One-Two Punch
cards.note: Response: after you make a basic attack using ATK, ready She-Hulk. The player basic-attack occurrence carries the attacking identity as actor and gains WhenAttackEnds only after the attack resolves, so an ability attack cannot satisfy this trigger.

cards.name: Split Personality
cards.note: Action: flip your identity, then draw up to the new face's printed hand size. rr:printed excludes hand-size modifiers, and rr:then makes the draw follow the form change rather than read the old face.

cards.name: Focused Rage
cards.note: Hero Action: exhaust Focused Rage and take 1 damage, then draw 1 card. Exhaustion and damage are costs before the arrow, so an exhausted upgrade or an identity prohibited from taking the damage cannot initiate the ability.

cards.name: War Machine
cards.note: Action: exhaust War Machine and deal 2 damage to him, then deal 1 damage to each enemy. Both costs must be payable before the effect; each current villain and engaged minion is damaged separately in deterministic board order.

cards.name: Black Widow
cards.note: Interrupt: when a card is revealed from the encounter deck, exhaust Black Widow and spend a mental resource to cancel that card's effects and discard it, then reveal the next card. The revealed card remains the occurrence subject throughout the interrupt.

cards.name: Program Transmitter
cards.note: Attach to Ultron. Its Forced Response places 1 threat on each side scheme after Ultron schemes. The Hero Action exhausts the resolving player's hero and spends two mental resources to discard this attachment.

cards.name: Repair Sequence
cards.note: When revealed, Ultron heals 2 damage per Drone engaged with the resolving player and gains surge only when the heal moved no damage. Its boost ability uses the same engaged Drone count but heals 1 per Drone.

cards.name: Rage of Ultron
cards.note: Ultron activates and the sentence resumes after that activation fully resolves. In alter-ego form, discard one player-deck card for each threat that activation placed; in hero form, discard one for each damage dealt by the attack's damage step.

cards.name: Vibranium Armor
cards.note: Attach to the villain. After the attached villain takes damage, its Forced Response gives it tough. The Hero Action exhausts the resolving player's hero and spends two physical resources to discard this attachment.

cards.name: Concussion Blasters
cards.note: Attach to the villain. The attached villain continuously gains retaliate 1. The Hero Action exhausts the resolving player's hero and spends two energy resources to discard this attachment.

cards.name: Hydra Soldier
cards.note: Guard is a printed keyword. When Hydra Soldier is defeated, its engaged player is dealt one facedown encounter card; the player comes from the minion's engaged play area, not from whichever effect dealt the final damage.

cards.name: Ultron
cards.note: After Ultron I attacks a player, that player chooses either 1 threat on the main scheme or one facedown Drone from the top of their deck. The completed attack occurrence identifies both Ultron as actor and the attacked player.

cards.name: Ultron
cards.note: When Ultron II attacks a player, his forced interrupt first creates one Drone engaged with that player, then grants Ultron +1 ATK per Drone now engaged with them until that attack ends.

cards.name: The Crimson Cowl
cards.note: When revealed, each player in player order creates one facedown Drone from the top of their own deck.

cards.name: Assault on NORAD
cards.note: When revealed, each player in player order creates one facedown Drone. Advancing to stage 2B is the generic main-scheme advance, not a second card ability.

cards.name: Countdown to Oblivion
cards.note: When revealed, each player in player order creates one facedown Drone. Advancing to stage 3B is the generic main-scheme advance.

cards.name: Ultron Drones
cards.note: The environment defines the facedown Drone card type, DRONE trait, and base SCH, ATK, and hit points. FacedownDrones and the defeat primitive apply those runtime semantics and return a defeated Drone to its original owner's discard pile; there is no second independently resolved tree on this face.

cards.name: Upgraded Drones
cards.note: Attach to the Ultron Drones environment. Every facedown Drone continuously gets +1 ATK and +1 hit point. A Hero Action spends one energy, one mental, and one physical resource to discard the attachment.

cards.name: Advanced Ultron Drone
cards.note: When this minion would be defeated, its forced interrupt creates a facedown Drone from the engaged player's deck. The engaged seat is read while this card is still in its engagement area.

cards.name: Swarm Attack
cards.note: When revealed in hero form, every facedown Drone engaged with the resolving player attacks in board order. The sentence waits for every activation and creates one Drone if none actually attacked, including when every attempted attack was canceled by stun. In alter-ego form it creates one immediately.

cards.name: Drone Factory
cards.note: When revealed, each player first creates a facedown Drone, then 1 threat is placed here for every Drone in play, including the ones just created.

cards.name: Invasive AI
cards.note: When revealed, each player discards the top three cards of their own deck in player order.

cards.name: Ultron's Imperative
cards.note: When revealed, the current first player creates two facedown Drones from the top of their deck.

cards.name: Jennifer Walters
cards.note: I Object! interrupts any imminent threat assignment and prevents 1 before it is placed. The once-per-round limit belongs to this alter-ego face's ability instance.

cards.name: Great Responsibility
cards.note: Hero Interrupt: replace an imminent threat assignment with the resolving hero taking the remaining amount as damage. The replacement removes the placement and closes its later windows.

cards.name: Emergency
cards.note: Interrupt (thwart): while the villain's scheme activation is assigning threat, prevent 1 of that assignment. The enemyScheme cause excludes villain-phase threat and the villain actor excludes minion schemes.

cards.name: Photonic Blast
cards.note: Hero Action (attack): choose an enemy and deal 5 attack damage. If any selected generator produced an energy or wild resource while paying for this event, draw 1 card after the damage.

cards.name: Relentless Assault
cards.note: Hero Action (attack): choose a minion and deal 5 attack damage. A physical or wild resource in the event's selected payment grants overkill to this one attack only.

cards.name: For Justice!
cards.note: Hero Action (thwart): choose a scheme and remove 3 threat, or 4 if any selected generator produced a mental or wild resource while paying for this event.

cards.name: Charge
cards.note: Attach to Rhino. [star] Forced Interrupt: When Rhino attacks, the attack gains overkill. At the end of this attack, discard Charge. The star sits in this card's ATK field, which rr:star-icon.2 makes a reminder to check the text box whenever the attached enemy uses that value to attack -- so this is an attachment ability while in play, not a 'Boost' ability. The printed ATK+ 3 is not here: rr:attachment.1 makes a printed modifier declarative, and StateFields reads it off the attachment without an ability. 'Rhino' is written as the villain in play because the card belongs to Rhino's encounter set and no other villain can share a table with it; a name query would need a lookup the printed data spells differently.

cards.name: "I'm Tough"
cards.note: When Revealed: Give Rhino a tough status card. If Rhino already has a tough status card, this card gains surge. The no-villain case is not printed and no rule covers it. **Our choice:** surge. A reveal that neither gives a status card nor surges is a card that does nothing at all, and rr:surge.1 is the branch the card already prints for 'the tough status card could not be given'. Both branches run: `giveStatus` is capped by rr:status-cards.1 and `gainSurge` deals one encounter card, which is rr:surge.1's 'When Revealed: deal yourself 1 facedown encounter card'.

cards.name: Advance
cards.note: When Revealed: The villain schemes. rr:scheme is the fifth basic power and this is the villain using it outside its own activation, so it is scheduled as a Scheme step rather than resolved here. It is a scheme however the revealing player's form would have activated the villain: rr:activation.1 decides the *scheduled* activation of the villain phase, and this card has already decided.

cards.name: Assault
cards.note: When Revealed (Alter-Ego): This card gains surge. When Revealed (Hero): The villain attacks you. Two printed abilities gated on form, written as one 'if' because the two forms are exclusive: the parenthesis is a condition on the ability rather than two abilities that could both apply. 'You' is the player revealing the card, which is the seat the When Revealed occurrence carries.

cards.name: Gang-Up
cards.note: When Revealed (Alter-Ego): This card gains surge. When Revealed (Hero): The villain and each minion engaged with you attacks you. Two activations rather than one attack by several enemies -- rr:attack-enemy-activation is one enemy's -- and a minion engaged with you attacking is the same thing villain phase step 2.b would have done. The order is the play area's, for the reason rr:minion.3 is taken that way there.

cards.name: Shocker
cards.note: When Revealed: Deal 1 damage to each hero. A minion, so the card also enters play; the ability is what the reveal resolves. 'Each hero' is not each identity -- rr:form-change-form.5 says abilities that interact with a player's hero do not interact with the identity of a player in alter-ego form, so a player who has flipped down takes nothing.

cards.name: Breakin' & Takin'
cards.note: When Revealed: Place an additional 1 [per_hero] threat here. 'Additional' is additional to the printed starting threat, which rr:side-scheme.1 has already placed by the time this resolves -- so this places only what the text says and does not restate the 2. 'Here' is the card itself. The hazard icon is a printed field and not this ability.

cards.name: Bomb Scare
cards.note: When Revealed: Place an additional 1 [per_hero] threat here. Word for word Breakin' & Takin', from a different encounter set; the acceleration icon rather than the hazard icon is the difference, and both are printed fields rather than abilities.

cards.name: Hard to Keep Down
cards.note: When Revealed: Rhino heals 4 damage. If no damage was healed this way, this card gains surge. The condition reads result.healed and not the villain's health, because rr:heal heals up to the amount: a villain damaged by 1 heals 1 and one at full health heals nothing, and a check made before the heal reads a number the heal may never reach. A villain that is not on the board heals nothing, which is the surge branch and not an error.

cards.name: False Alarm
cards.note: When Revealed: You are confused. If you are already confused, this card gains surge. 'You' is a card here and not a player: rr:you-your.5 says a status card placed on 'you' goes on the resolving player's identity. Written as if/else on the same shape as 01105 -- rr:status-cards.1 caps a character at one card of each type, so the two branches are exclusive in fact as well as in the sentence.

cards.name: Klaw
cards.note: Forced Interrupt: when Klaw attacks, give him one additional boost card. The interrupt resolves while Klaw is the attack actor, before the ordinary boost-card step, and additional boost cards are cumulative.

cards.name: Klaw
cards.note: Forced Interrupt: when Klaw attacks, give him one additional boost card. When revealed, search the encounter deck and discard pile for The Immortal Klaw and reveal it; the search primitive shuffles the searched encounter deck.

cards.name: Klaw
cards.note: Forced Interrupt: when Klaw attacks, give him one additional boost card. Toughness is a printed keyword handled by the generic enters-play keyword rules.

cards.name: Hydra Bomber
cards.note: When Revealed: Choose to either take 2 damage or place 1 threat on the main scheme. rr:choose-game-element.1 asks the player resolving the ability, which for a revealed encounter card is the player it was dealt to. rr:you-your.2 makes 'take 2 damage' damage to that player's identity. Neither option needs a target beyond one that is always there, so rr:choose-option.1 -- an encounter card cannot offer an option with no valid target -- never bites here.

cards.name: Rhino
cards.note: Stage I. No text at all: the printed HP, ATK, SCH and the Boost field are attributes rather than abilities, and rr:attachment.1 makes the printed modifiers on what is attached to him declarative too. Read and empty, which is not the same as unread.

cards.name: Hydra Mercenary
cards.note: Guard, and nothing else. rr:guard is a keyword the engine reads off the printed field -- see docs/keywords.md -- so there is no ability here to author.

cards.name: Sandman
cards.note: Toughness, and nothing else. rr:toughness gives the minion a tough status card as it enters play, which Reveal.EnterPlay does from the printed keyword.

cards.name: Crowd Control
cards.note: A crisis icon and no text. rr:crisis-icon.1 makes the icon 'equivalent to the following constant ability: player cards cannot remove threat from the main scheme', and the engine reads it off the printed field in BasicPowers -- a constant ability is not a triggered one and has nothing to wait for.

cards.name: The Break-In!
cards.note: Stage 1B. 'If this stage is completed, the players lose the game' is rr:main-scheme-main-scheme-deck.2.1 restated on the card, and the engine answers it in Threat.Completed: an empty main scheme deck under a completed scheme is the villain winning. Nothing here to trigger.

cards.name: Caught Off Guard
cards.note: When Revealed: Discard an upgrade or support you control. If no cards were discarded this way, this card gains surge. Written as if/else on whether there is a legal discard target, rather than as a discard followed by a check: the instruction is mandatory, so 'no cards were discarded this way' happens exactly when there was nothing legal to discard. The discardable selector applies Permanent target legality to both the condition and the prompt. That also keeps the choice last in its branch, which is what the interpreter can resume. rr:choose-game-element.1 asks the player resolving the card, which is the player it was dealt to.

cards.name: Rhino
cards.note: Stage II. When Revealed: Search the encounter deck and discard pile for the Breakin' & Takin' side scheme and reveal it. Shuffle the encounter deck. The final sentence is rr:search.3 restated -- 'if any portion of a deck is searched, upon completion of that card ability, shuffle that entire deck' -- so it is the node's own doing rather than a second instruction. The discard pile is searched and not shuffled, because it is not a deck. Named by printed id because the card names a specific card and rr:identity.2 makes a title refer to one card.

cards.name: Exhaustion
cards.note: Surge. When Revealed: Exhaust your identity card. The surge is a printed keyword the engine already reads, so the ability is the one sentence. 'Your identity card' is rr:you-your again -- the resolving player's identity, whichever face is showing, and rr:form-change-form.2 keeps the exhausted state across a flip.

cards.name: Under Fire
cards.note: Surge. When Revealed: Reveal the top card of the encounter deck. Revealed and not dealt -- rr:deal-deal-an-encounter-card puts a card facedown in a queue for the next villain phase, and this one is turned over now. The surge deals a card as well, so this treachery costs two: one revealed at once and one queued.

cards.name: Shadow of the Past
cards.note: When Revealed: Reveal your set-aside nemesis minion and put it into play engaged with you. Reveal your set-aside nemesis side scheme and put it into play. Shuffle the rest of your set-aside nemesis encounter set into the encounter deck. If your nemesis minion does not enter the game this way, this card gains surge. The card appears in every supported Core Set scenario. 'Put into play engaged with you' and 'put it into play' are both rr:reveal.step.2 by card type, so both are a reveal rather than a placement. The two reveals happen before the shuffle so that the cards they take are no longer among 'the rest'; the obligation is not among them either, because setup shuffled it into the encounter deck long before this resolves.

cards.name: Masterplan
cards.note: When Revealed: Place 4 threat on each side scheme. If there are no side schemes in play, discard cards from the top of the encounter deck until a side scheme is discarded. Reveal that side scheme. Written as if/else because the sentence is one: 'each side scheme' when there are any, the search when there are none. 'Each side scheme' reaches the players' as well as the scenario's -- rr:player-side-scheme calls them the player card equivalent and .1 puts them in the same place. Four threat flat, not per player.

cards.name: Vulture
cards.note: Quickstrike, and nothing else. Spider-Man's nemesis minion, brought in by Shadow of the Past. rr:quickstrike is a keyword the engine reads off the printed field, so there is no ability here to author.

cards.name: Stampede
cards.note: When Revealed (Alter-Ego): This card gains surge. When Revealed (Hero): Rhino attacks you. If a character is damaged by this attack, that character is stunned. The second sentence is a delayed effect and not a response: rr:delayed-effect.1 resolves it immediately after the condition becomes true and before responses to it may be used, and rr:delayed-effect.2 says it is not a new triggered ability. The character it stuns does not exist when the effect is made -- the attack has not happened -- so the occurrence names it when it comes due. rr:tough.3 is why 'damaged' is not 'attacked': a character whose tough status card ate the damage is not considered to have taken damage, and is not stunned.

cards.name: Sweeping Swoop
cards.note: When Revealed: Stun your hero. If Vulture is in play, this card gains surge. [star] Boost: If this activation deals damage to a friendly character, stun that character. Two abilities at two tiers on one card, which is why the boost guard asks whether *this half* is written rather than whether the card is. 'Your hero' is not 'you': rr:form-change-form.5 says abilities that interact with a player's hero do not interact with the identity of a player in alter-ego form, so an alter-ego is not stunned -- and the surge branch is a separate sentence that still applies. The boost half is bounded by the end of the activation rather than the end of the attack, because a scheme is an activation too and an effect that outlived one would fire during somebody else's attack. Every character an enemy activation damages is friendly, so the boost's 'friendly' needs no filter of its own; a card that damages an enemy this way would.

cards.name: Aunt May
cards.note: Alter-Ego Action: Exhaust Aunt May -> heal 4 damage from Peter Parker. The first card in the dataset with a cost, and the first with an action. rr:player-turn.5.1 is the 'Alter-Ego' in front of it: the player must be in that form to trigger it, which is the trigger's 'form'. rr:initiating-abilities keeps the steps apart, so the exhaust is the ability's cost rather than the first thing its effect does -- and rr:exhausted.2 is why an already-exhausted Aunt May is not offered at all. 'Peter Parker' is the player's identity: the card is in their play area and rr:you-your resolves the alter-ego by title to the identity showing it.

cards.name: Enhanced Ivory Horn
cards.note: Attach to Rhino. Hero Action: Spend [physical] [physical] [physical] resources -> discard this card. An encounter card in play, so rr:player-turn.5.b is what lets a player trigger it -- it is nobody's card and everybody's action. The printed ATK+ 1 is not here: rr:attachment.1 makes a printed modifier declarative and StateFields reads it off the attachment without an ability. The spend is the ability's cost rather than the first thing its effect does, which is why rr:initiating-abilities.step.3 can refuse to offer it to a hand that cannot pay.

cards.name: The Vulture's Plans
cards.note: When Revealed: Discard 1 card at random from each player's hand. Place 1 threat on the main scheme for each different resource type discarded this way. 'Each player' goes in player order -- rr:each-player.1 -- and that order is what the random stream sees, so it is a wire fact rather than a tidiness. 'Each different resource type' counts distinct letters among what was discarded: a card printing two of one letter is one type and a card printing none is none, so the threat is between zero and four however many players there are.

cards.name: Eviction Notice
cards.note: Give to the Peter Parker player. You may flip to alter-ego form. Choose: exhaust Peter Parker to remove Eviction Notice from the game, or discard 1 card at random from your hand, this card gains surge, discard this obligation. Two questions in a row, which is the shape the interpreter had to learn to resume for. rr:form-change-form.3 is why the flip does not use up the turn's: 'if a card ability causes a player to change forms, it does not count against the one voluntary form change'. rr:obligation.1 makes 'you' the player whose play area the obligation is in, which rr:obligation.4 makes the Peter Parker player -- the same seat as the revealing player at one player, and MARVEL-225 above two. The first option's exhaust is written as its effect rather than as a cost because rr:choose-option.1 bars an encounter card's option only for want of a target, not for want of a cost.

cards.name: Explosion
cards.note: When Revealed: If Bomb Scare is in play, assign X damage among heroes and allies, where X is the amount of threat on Bomb Scare. If Bomb Scare is not in play, this card gains surge. X is read off the board rather than printed -- rr:threat counts tokens -- so it is the threat pool on the card named by title. The assignment is rr:indirect-damage: .2 divides it among friendly characters in play, .3 assigns the whole lot before resolving any of it, and .3.1 caps each character at its remaining hit points. Only two cards in the pool say 'assign ... among' and the other one says 'indirect' outright; this one does not, but the division it describes is the same one.

cards.name: Highway Robbery
cards.note: When Revealed: Each player places a random card from their hand facedown here. When Defeated: Return each facedown card here to its owner's hand. Placed and not discarded -- the cards come back, which is what the second ability is for -- so they go onto the scheme as attachments, facedown. 'Its owner's hand' is the card's owner and not whoever defeated the scheme, which is why each player gets their own card back. rr:when-defeated-abilities.2.1 runs the return before the scheme leaves play, which is what lets it still find what is attached to it.

cards.name: Armored Rhino Suit
cards.note: Attach to Rhino. Forced Interrupt: When any amount of damage would be dealt to Rhino, place it here instead. Then, if there is at least 5 damage here, discard Armored Rhino Suit. A replacement effect -- rr:replacement-effect's 'when [triggering condition] would happen, do [replacement effect] instead' -- sitting at rr:damage.step.1, which is before the tough card at step 2. 'Place it here' is placing and not dealing: the damage goes on as tokens rather than starting the nine steps again on a card that is not a character. The subject is the attached card rather than this one, because it is Rhino being dealt the damage.

cards.name: Rhino
cards.note: Stage III, which only the expert villain deck reaches. Toughness is a printed keyword rather than an ability -- rr:toughness.1 spells it out as a Forced Response and Reveal.EnterPlay is where the engine keeps it -- so the When Revealed is all there is to author. 'Each hero' is rr:form-change-form.5: while a player is in alter-ego form, card abilities that interact with their hero do not interact with their identity, so a table that has flipped down takes nothing.

cards.name: The Break-In!
cards.note: Main scheme stage 1, the A side. Its printed text is the scenario's contents list and one setup line, 'Advance to stage 1B.' Neither is an ability this card runs: the contents say what to put in the box before the game, and the advance is the setup step itself. rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.12.b flips the main scheme to side 1B for every scenario, and the engine does it there -- so this line is that rule restated on the card, in the same category as 01097b's 'the players lose the game'. It is deliberately not authored as a Setup ability: running it at step 12a would advance the scheme and step 12b would then advance it again, off the end of a deck that has one stage in it. Sixty-two main schemes in the pool print the clause and the appendix covers all of them. rr:main-scheme-main-scheme-deck.step.2 and .step.3 are the same two-sided reveal for a stage the deck advances to, and 01097b is where that side's text lives. Read and empty, which is not the same as unread.

cards.name: The Doomsday Chair
cards.note: When Revealed: If M.O.D.O.K. is not in play, search the encounter deck and discard pile for M.O.D.O.K. and put him into play engaged with you, then shuffle the encounter deck. The title check reads only in-play areas, so a copy in either searched out-of-play area does not suppress the effect. rr:search.1 makes a matching card the player's choice if more than one exists; the core set has one M.O.D.O.K., and singular cardsIn refuses rather than guesses if a future board produces several. rr:search.2 leaves every card where it is until putIntoPlay moves the match. rr:search.3 requires the encounter deck shuffle even when no match exists, so both branches say it. And rr:when-revealed-abilities.2 is why the move is putIntoPlay rather than reveal: a When Revealed ability on M.O.D.O.K. would not trigger, while rr:enters-play still applies its printed keywords.

cards.name: M.O.D.O.K.
cards.note: Retaliate 2. The card has no authored ability because Retaliate is a printed keyword read by the rules engine. rr:retaliate-x makes it a Forced Response after this character is attacked, and rr:retaliate-x.2 requires M.O.D.O.K. to remain in play after the attack resolves.

cards.name: Biomechanical Upgrades
cards.note: Surge. Attach to the minion with the highest printed hit points and without another Biomechanical Upgrades attached. Forced Interrupt: When attached minion would be defeated, heal all damage from it instead, then discard this card. The surge is a printed keyword the reveal rule reads. The attachment selector uses printed HP rather than modified HP; the official ruling in datasets/marvelcdb-faq/faq.json says base stats on a facedown Ultron drone count as printed and '+ stats' do not. rr:first-player.1 gives a tied highest target to the first player, which the engine refuses until attachment selection can ask. rr:damage.step.6 places this interrupt after damage is placed and before defeat, so healing all damage invalidates the imminent defeat under rr:would.1. The final discard then removes this copy from play under rr:attach-to.1.

cards.name: Energy Absorption
cards.note: This resource card has no ability. Its three printed energy resources are read from datasets/cards by the resource rules.

cards.name: Black Panther
cards.note: Retaliate 1 is a printed keyword read by the rules engine, so this face has no authored ability.

cards.name: Vibranium
cards.note: This resource card has no ability. Its two printed wild resources are read from datasets/cards by the resource rules.

cards.name: Luke Cage
cards.note: Toughness is a printed keyword read when this ally enters play, so this card has no authored ability.

cards.name: Energy
cards.note: This resource card has no ability. Its two printed energy resources are read from datasets/cards by the resource rules.

cards.name: Genius
cards.note: This resource card has no ability. Its two printed mental resources are read from datasets/cards by the resource rules.

cards.name: Strength
cards.note: This resource card has no ability. Its two printed physical resources are read from datasets/cards by the resource rules.

cards.name: Secret Rendezvous
cards.note: This final main-scheme stage has no card ability. Completing the final stage makes the villain win under rr:main-scheme-main-scheme-deck.2.1, which the main-scheme rule applies generically.

cards.name: Armored Guard
cards.note: Guard and Toughness are printed keywords read by the rules engine, so this minion has no authored ability.

cards.name: Usurp The Throne
cards.note: The card prints only a hazard icon and no ability. The icon is read from datasets/cards.

cards.name: Whiplash
cards.note: Retaliate 1 is a printed keyword read by the rules engine, so this minion has no authored ability.

cards.name: Spider-Woman
cards.note: Response: after Spider-Woman enters play, confuse the villain. Putting her into play also satisfies the printed condition; the response remains optional under rr:response.

cards.name: Hellcat
cards.note: Action: return Hellcat to your hand. The card moves from its controller's ally area to its owner's hand.

cards.name: Ground Stomp
cards.note: Hero Action: deal 1 damage to each enemy. rr:enemy includes the villain and every minion in play, and each damage instance goes through the damage rule.

cards.name: Superhuman Law Division
cards.note: Alter-Ego Action: exhaust this support and spend a mental resource to remove 2 threat from a scheme. The two costs are paid before the chosen scheme is changed under rr:initiating-abilities.

cards.name: Mark V Armor
cards.note: You get +6 hit points. The constant modifies the controlling identity's maximum hit points through the same field Damage.Health reads.

cards.name: Rocket Boots
cards.note: You get +1 hit point. Its Hero Action exhausts the boots and spends a mental resource to give the controlling identity AERIAL until the end of the phase.

cards.name: The Golden City
cards.note: Alter-Ego Action: exhaust The Golden City to draw 2 cards.

cards.name: Uppercut
cards.note: Hero Action: deal 5 damage to an enemy.

cards.name: Tac Team
cards.note: Uses 3 attack counters is a printed keyword. Its Action exhausts the support and removes one counter to deal 2 damage to an enemy.

cards.name: Combat Training
cards.note: The controlling player's hero gets +1 ATK. The play-under-control instruction is handled by card play; this constant reads the current controller's hero.

cards.name: Surveillance Team
cards.note: Uses 3 snoop counters is a printed keyword. Its Action exhausts the support and removes one counter to remove 1 threat from a scheme.

cards.name: Heroic Intuition
cards.note: The controlling player's hero gets +1 THW. The play-under-control instruction is handled by card play.

cards.name: Vision
cards.note: Spend an energy resource to choose THW or ATK; Vision gets +2 to that power until the end of the phase, once per round.

cards.name: Inspired
cards.note: Attach to an ally. The attached ally gets +1 THW and +1 ATK while this upgrade remains attached.

cards.name: Get Behind Me!
cards.note: Hero Interrupt: cancel a revealed treachery's When Revealed effects, then make the villain attack the resolving player instead. The revealed card itself remains revealed under rr:cancel.4.

cards.name: Med Team
cards.note: Uses 3 medical counters is a printed keyword. Its Action exhausts the support and removes one counter to heal 2 damage from a friendly character.

cards.name: Armored Vest
cards.note: The controlling player's hero gets +1 DEF. The play-under-control instruction is handled by card play.

cards.name: Mockingbird
cards.note: Response: after Mockingbird enters play, stun an enemy. The response asks the resolving player which enemy receives the status.

cards.name: Haymaker
cards.note: Hero Action: deal 3 damage to an enemy.

cards.name: Solid-Sound Body
cards.note: Attach to Klaw. Klaw gains retaliate 1 while attached. A Hero Action spends one resource of each type to discard the attachment.

cards.name: Weapons Runner
cards.note: Surge is a printed keyword resolved by reveal. Its Boost ability puts this card into play engaged with the attacked player rather than discarding it with the other boost cards.

cards.name: Sound Manipulation
cards.note: The alter-ego branch heals Klaw for 4 and gains surge when nothing was healed. The hero branch deals 2 damage to the resolving identity and heals Klaw for 2.

cards.name: Klaw's Vengeance
cards.note: In alter-ego form, discard one random card from your hand. In hero form, Klaw attacks you; the sentence resumes only after that activation fully resolves, and places one threat on the main scheme only if the attack's damage step dealt damage.

cards.name: Sonic Boom
cards.note: When revealed, choose either to spend one energy, one mental, and one physical resource or exhaust every character you control; the resource option is offered only when payable. As a boost card it registers an effect against the current activation and exhausts your hero after completion if that activation dealt damage to you.

cards.name: Defense Network
cards.note: When revealed, place 1 additional threat per player here. The card's printed starting threat is applied separately when it enters play.

cards.name: Illegal Arms Factory
cards.note: When revealed, place 1 additional threat per player here. The card's printed starting threat is applied separately when it enters play.

cards.name: The "Immortal" Klaw
cards.note: Klaw gets +10 hit points while this side scheme remains in play. Defeating the scheme removes the constant modifier automatically.

cards.name: Radioactive Man
cards.note: After Radioactive Man attacks the resolving player, discard one card at random from that player's hand. Its Boost ability does the same immediately.

cards.name: Tiger Shark
cards.note: After Tiger Shark attacks, give him tough. Its Boost ability gives the activating villain tough.

cards.name: Concussive Blast
cards.note: When revealed, deal 1 damage to each friendly character. Its Boost ability deals 1 damage to each character controlled by the attacked player.

cards.name: Heart-Shaped Herb
cards.note: Surge is a printed keyword. When revealed, give the villain and every minion engaged with the resolving player tough; its Boost ability gives the villain tough.

cards.name: Personal Challenge
cards.note: When revealed, place 1 additional threat per player here.

cards.name: Genetically Enhanced
cards.note: Attach to a minion with the highest printed hit points. If none is in play, gain surge. The attached minion gets +3 hit points while this attachment remains.

cards.name: Imminent Overload
cards.note: When revealed, place 1 additional threat per player here.

cards.name: The Psyche-Magnitron
cards.note: When revealed, place 1 additional threat per player here.

cards.name: Yon-Rogg
cards.note: After Yon-Rogg attacks, place 1 threat on The Psyche-Magnitron if that side scheme is in play.

cards.name: Countdown to Oblivion
cards.note: Threat cannot be removed from this scheme. rr:cannot makes the prohibition absolute, so both basic thwarts and card effects ask it before removing threat. Completing this final stage is handled generically by rr:main-scheme-main-scheme-deck.2.1.

cards.name: Carol Danvers
cards.note: Commander — Action: choose a player to draw 1 card, limited once per round. Identities stand for players when the table asks the resolving player to choose one.

cards.name: Alpha Flight Station
cards.note: The exhaust and chosen discard are costs. The resolving player draws 2 cards as Carol Danvers and 1 otherwise.

cards.name: Captain Marvel's Helmet
cards.note: Captain Marvel gets +2 DEF while she has AERIAL and +1 DEF otherwise. The current trait includes traits granted by lasting effects.

cards.name: Gamma Slam
cards.note: The attack deals damage equal to the hero's sustained damage, capped at 15.

cards.name: Iron Man
cards.note: Iron Man's printed hand size is 1. He gets +1 hand size for each TECH upgrade he controls, including a currently granted TECH trait, capped at a total hand size of 7.

cards.name: Repulsor Blast
cards.note: The chosen enemy takes 1 damage, then the top 5 player-deck cards are discarded. Each one with a printed energy resource adds 2 damage to that same enemy.

cards.name: Supersonic Punch
cards.note: The attack deals 8 damage while Iron Man has AERIAL and 4 damage otherwise.

cards.name: Arc Reactor
cards.note: Its Hero Action exhausts Arc Reactor as its cost and readies Iron Man.

cards.name: Powered Gauntlets
cards.note: The Hero Action exhausts the gauntlets, then deals 2 damage while Iron Man has AERIAL and 1 otherwise.

cards.name: Jessica Jones
cards.note: Jessica Jones gets +1 THW for each side scheme in play.

cards.name: Get Ready
cards.note: The action chooses and readies an ally.

cards.name: The Triskelion
cards.note: This support increases its controller's ally limit by 1 while it is in play.

cards.name: First Aid
cards.note: The action chooses any character and heals 2 damage from it.

cards.name: Avengers Mansion
cards.note: The action exhausts the support, chooses a player through that player's identity, and has that player draw 1 card.

cards.name: Lead from the Front
cards.note: The Hero Action chooses a player through that player's identity. Every character that player controls gets +1 THW and +1 ATK until the end of the player phase; the live lasting-effect scope also reaches a character that enters under that player's control later in the phase, as rr:lasting-effects.4 requires.

cards.name: Make the Call
cards.note: The Action offers each affordable ally in every player's discard pile, priced at that ally's printed resource cost from the resolving player's generators. The chosen exact card keeps its owner but enters the resolving player's ally area under their control; putting it into play is not playing it and therefore does not spend next-card cost reductions or produce a Card Played response.

cards.name: Helicarrier
cards.note: The Action exhausts Helicarrier and chooses a player through that player's identity. A one-use lasting effect reduces the next card that player successfully plays this phase by 1; pricing an offer does not consume it, and an unused reduction expires at the end of the player phase.

cards.name: Tenacity
cards.note: The Hero Action spends a physical resource and discards Tenacity as its costs, then readies the player's hero.

cards.name: Mark V Helmet
cards.note: Its Hero Action exhausts the helmet. With AERIAL it removes 1 threat from every scheme; otherwise it removes 1 from one chosen scheme.

cards.name: Maria Hill
cards.note: After Maria Hill enters play, her optional response has each player draw 1 card in player order.

cards.name: Nick Fury
cards.note: After Nick Fury enters play, choose one printed effect. The same response records the delayed end-of-round discard, which does nothing if he has already left play.

cards.name: Underground Distribution
cards.note: Setup searches the encounter deck for Defense Network and reveals it. The search primitive shuffles the searched encounter deck under rr:search.3. The contents list is scenario setup data, and rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.12.b performs the printed advance to 1B.

cards.name: Underground Distribution
cards.note: When revealed, discard from the encounter deck until a minion is discarded, then put that exact minion into play engaged with the first player. Put into play is deliberately not reveal: rr:when-revealed-abilities.2 leaves the minion's own When Revealed ability inactive, while rr:enters-play still applies its printed enters-play keywords.

cards.name: Secret Rendezvous
cards.note: When revealed, discard from the encounter deck until a minion is discarded and put that exact minion into play engaged with the first player. The printed advance to 2B is the main-scheme stage transition rather than a second card effect.

cards.name: The Masters of Evil
cards.note: When revealed, discard from the encounter deck until a printed MASTERS_OF_EVIL minion is discarded, then put that exact minion into play engaged with the first player. The trait is read from the out-of-play printed face, where rr:ability leaves continuous trait grants inactive.

cards.name: Legal Work
cards.note: The obligation may flip Jennifer Walters to alter-ego, then chooses between exhausting her to remove Legal Work from the game or placing one permanent acceleration token beside the main scheme and discarding the obligation. The two printed choices are two sequential questions, as on the other core obligations.

cards.name: The Crimson Cowl
cards.note: Setup puts the set-aside Ultron Drones environment into its printed in-play destination without revealing it, then performs the printed encounter-deck shuffle. The contents list is scenario setup data, and rr:appendix-ii-setup.step.12.b performs the printed advance to 1B.

cards.name: Kree Manipulator
cards.note: Surge is a printed keyword. When revealed it places 1 threat on the main scheme; as a boost card it does so only during an undefended attack.

cards.name: Affairs of State
cards.note: The obligation may flip T'Challa to alter-ego, then chooses between exhausting him to remove it from the game or discarding a controlled BLACK PANTHER upgrade and this obligation.

cards.name: Business Problems
cards.note: The obligation may flip Tony Stark to alter-ego, then chooses between exhausting him to remove it from the game or exhausting every controlled upgrade and discarding the obligation.

cards.name: Family Emergency
cards.note: The obligation may flip Carol Danvers to alter-ego, then chooses between exhausting her to remove it from the game or stunning her, gaining surge, and discarding the obligation.

cards.name: Sonic Converter
cards.note: It attaches to Klaw. After the attached Klaw attacks and damages a character, the forced response stuns that target. Its Hero Action spends one of each named resource to discard the attachment.

cards.name: Electric Whip Attack
cards.note: When revealed, choose between damage equal to the controlled upgrade count or discarding a chosen controlled upgrade. Its Boost ability discards a chosen upgrade only during an undefended attack.

cards.name: Legions of Hydra
cards.note: When revealed, it puts Madame Hydra into play from the encounter deck or discard pile if she is absent, shuffles the encounter deck, then places 2 additional threat for each HYDRA enemy in play.

cards.name: Titania
cards.note: Titania's attack value is X, continuously equal to her current remaining hit points: modified maximum health minus damage sustained.

cards.name: Titania's Fury
cards.note: When revealed in hero form, Titania attacks and the sentence resumes after the activation; if she did not actually attack, heal all damage from her and gain surge. In alter-ego form no attack can be initiated, so that fallback resolves immediately. Its Boost ability gives the activating villain one additional boost card.

cards.name: Ultron
cards.note: Each facedown Drone minion gets +1 ATK and +1 hit point. Ultron cannot take damage while any Drone is in play. When revealed, this stage searches for Ultron's Imperative by printed id and reveals it, shuffling the encounter deck as search requires.

cards.name: Killmonger
cards.note: Killmonger cannot take damage whose source is an Upgrade carrying the BLACK PANTHER trait. Other sources damage him normally.

cards.name: Madame Hydra
cards.note: Madame Hydra cannot take damage from any source while Legions of Hydra is in play. After one of her completed attacks or schemes, a single combined forced response places two threat on Legions of Hydra; a canceled activation does not satisfy 'after she attacks or schemes'.

cards.name: Crisis Interdiction
cards.note: The hero action chooses its first scheme and, when Captain Marvel is AERIAL and a different scheme exists, a second different scheme in one ordered target request. It removes two threat from each chosen scheme, preserving which target is first and preventing the second from repeating it.

cards.name: Ancestral Knowledge
cards.note: The alter-ego action chooses one to three cards with different titles from the resolving player's discard pile, moves those exact cards into the player deck, and shuffles once after all moves.

cards.name: She-Hulk
cards.note: After the identity changes to this hero face, the optional response chooses an enemy and deals two damage. The FormChanged occurrence is scheduled only after the new face is showing, so the alter-ego face cannot answer it.

cards.name: T'Challa
cards.note: Foresight resolves at setup step 16 after mulligans and before round one. It searches the resolving player's deck for a BLACK_PANTHER upgrade, lets that player choose the exact match to add to hand, and shuffles the searched deck even when no match remains.

cards.name: Energy Channel
cards.note: Its first Action spends a player-chosen positive number X of energy or wild resources and places exactly that many energy counters. Its separate Hero Action (attack) discards Energy Channel as its cost, chooses an enemy, and deals twice the stored counters capped at 10 damage. The two same-tier actions carry distinct ordinals so the action prompt and resolver preserve which printed ability was chosen.

cards.name: Shuri
cards.note: After Shuri enters play, her optional response searches the controlling player's deck for an Upgrade. The player chooses among every matching card, adds it to hand, then shuffles the searched deck.

cards.name: Hawkeye
cards.note: Hawkeye enters play with four arrow counters before the entry response window opens. After a minion enters play, his optional response removes one arrow counter as its cost and deals two damage to that entered minion.

cards.name: Tony Stark
cards.note: Futurist looks at the current top three cards in top-to-bottom order. The player chooses one to add to hand and the other looked-at cards are discarded; the action is limited to once per round.

cards.name: Pepper Potts
cards.note: The resource ability exhausts Pepper Potts and dynamically generates the printed resource string of the current top card of her controller's discard pile. With no top card it is not an available generator.

cards.name: Stark Tower
cards.note: The alter-ego action exhausts Stark Tower, chooses a player who has a TECH upgrade in their discard pile, and returns the topmost matching upgrade to that card's owner's hand. Cards above it that are not TECH stay where they are.

cards.name: Superhuman Strength
cards.note: She-Hulk gets +2 ATK. After her attack completes, the forced response discards this upgrade and stuns that attack's target.

cards.name: Wakanda Forever!
cards.note: Hero Action: choose one permutation of every BLACK PANTHER upgrade you control, then resolve their Special abilities in exactly that order. The queued final member is marked as the final step of the sequence.

cards.name: Wakanda Forever!
cards.note: Hero Action: choose one permutation of every BLACK PANTHER upgrade you control, then resolve their Special abilities in exactly that order. The queued final member is marked as the final step of the sequence.

cards.name: Wakanda Forever!
cards.note: Hero Action: choose one permutation of every BLACK PANTHER upgrade you control, then resolve their Special abilities in exactly that order. The queued final member is marked as the final step of the sequence.

cards.name: Wakanda Forever!
cards.note: Hero Action: choose one permutation of every BLACK PANTHER upgrade you control, then resolve their Special abilities in exactly that order. The queued final member is marked as the final step of the sequence.

cards.name: Energy Daggers
cards.note: Special: choose a player, then deal the same amount to the villain before each enemy engaged with that player. That order preserves the simultaneous-damage ruling for Ultron III: his Drone prohibition is checked while the Drone is still in play. The amount is two only for the final step.

cards.name: Panther Claws
cards.note: Special (attack): choose an enemy and deal two damage, or four when this is the final step. The upgrade is the damage source.

cards.name: Tactical Genius
cards.note: Special (thwart): choose a scheme and remove one threat, or two when this is the final step.

cards.name: Vibranium Suit
cards.note: Special (attack): choose an enemy and move one damage from your hero to it, or two when final. The suit is the damage source, so source-based prohibitions can prevent the move before damage leaves the hero.

cards.name: Hulk
cards.note: After Hulk attacks, discard the top player-deck card. Its printed resource independently applies each matching line; a wild resource applies all three.

cards.name: Tigra
cards.note: After Tigra attacks and that same attack defeats its minion target, the optional response heals 1 damage from her before consequential damage is applied.

cards.name: Chase Them Down
cards.note: After the player's hero attacks and that attack defeats its enemy target, the response chooses a scheme and removes 2 threat.

cards.name: Daredevil
cards.note: After Daredevil thwarts a scheme, his response chooses an enemy and deals 1 damage before consequential damage is applied.

cards.name: Interrogation Room
cards.note: After a character controlled by this support's controller defeats a minion, its response exhausts the support and removes 1 threat from a chosen scheme.

cards.name: Counter-Punch
cards.note: After the player's hero uses its basic defense against an enemy attack, this attack response deals that hero's modified ATK damage to the attacking enemy.

cards.name: Indomitable
cards.note: After the player's hero uses its basic defense, the optional response discards this upgrade and readies that hero.

cards.name: Whirlwind
cards.note: When Whirlwind attacks, his forced interrupt adds every other non-eliminated hero as a target of this same attack in seat order; it does not initiate additional attacks or deal additional boost cards. As a boost card, deal one damage to each hero.

cards.name: Masters of Mayhem
cards.note: Each MASTERS_OF_EVIL minion engaged with a hero attacks that own engaged hero, so the batch can span seats. The sentence resumes after every activation and, if none actually attacked, the resolving player chooses a matching minion from the encounter deck or discard pile, puts it into play engaged with them, and shuffles the searched encounter deck.

cards.name: Melter
cards.note: The engaged player must defend Melter's attacks with a ready ally they control if one can legally defend; otherwise the ordinary defender choices remain optional. The Boost ability exhausts every ally controlled by the resolving player.

cards.name: Legal Practice
cards.note: Alter-Ego Action (thwart): choose a threatened scheme and one to five other cards in hand, discard those cards, and remove one threat per card actually discarded. The event itself is being played and is not one of the cards in hand available to choose.

cards.name: Assault on NORAD
cards.note: After villain phase step one finishes placing threat, each player in player order independently chooses either two more threat here or one facedown Drone from the top of their own deck. Each player's choice resolves in a fresh frame so 'their deck' remains that player's deck through the question.

cards.name: Android Efficiency
cards.note: When revealed, each player in player order creates a Drone from their own deck. Its boost ability makes the attacked player either spend one energy resource or create a Drone from that player's deck.

cards.name: Android Efficiency
cards.note: When revealed, each player in player order creates a Drone from their own deck. Its boost ability makes the attacked player either spend one mental resource or create a Drone from that player's deck.

cards.name: Android Efficiency
cards.note: When revealed, each player in player order creates a Drone from their own deck. Its boost ability makes the attacked player either spend one physical resource or create a Drone from that player's deck.

cards.name: Under Attack
cards.note: When revealed, each player in player order independently chooses either two threat here or three damage to their own hero. Fresh per-player frames keep both 'their hero' and the chosen branch bound to the player answering.

cards.name: Ritual Combat
cards.note: When revealed, discard exactly the top encounter card, then choose damage to the resolving hero or threat on the main scheme. X is read from that immediately discarded card as one plus its printed boost value.

cards.name: Electromagnetic Backlash
cards.note: Each player in player order discards the top five cards of their own deck and takes one damage per printed energy resource among their own discarded cards. Printed double-resource cards therefore count twice.

cards.name: Yon-Rogg's Treason
cards.note: Discard every card with a printed energy resource from the resolving player's hand. If that discarded no cards, the treachery gains surge; a double-energy card is still one discarded card for this condition.

cards.name: The Power of Aggression
cards.note: This card generates one wild resource normally and doubles that output while paying for an Aggression card. The card being paid for is payment context supplied by the engine, not inferred from the hand.

cards.name: The Power of Justice
cards.note: This card generates one wild resource normally and doubles that output while paying for a Justice card.

cards.name: The Power of Leadership
cards.note: This card generates one wild resource normally and doubles that output while paying for a Leadership card.

cards.name: The Power of Protection
cards.note: This card generates one wild resource normally and doubles that output while paying for a Protection card.
